instruction: Generate PDF versions of the opened blog articles in the browser and place them in /home/user/Downloads/BlogPosts, with filenames matching the article titles.

parameters.command: timeout 2 bash -c 'while ! curl -s http://localhost:9222/json > /dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 0.5; done' || true

metadata.explanation: Task requires exporting 2 Chrome tabs to PDF files in /home/user/Downloads/BlogPosts directory. The evaluator checks if 2 PDFs exist and their filenames contain keywords from the article titles ('agent' and 'human').

llm_judge_reasons: ✅ Title extraction is now reliable: Getter uses Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) on port 9222 to extract actual page titles from Chrome tabs, which is the correct approach for getting real article titles.

✅ Fallback mechanism is appropriate: If CDP fails, falls back to accessibility tree extraction, and only fails verification (returns empty article_titles) if both methods fail, which is semantically correct.
✅ Improved matching threshold: Metric now uses 0.7 threshold (increased from 0.5) and requires at least 2 significant words from the title to be present in the filename, reducing false positives.
✅ Complete requirement coverage: Evaluator checks all three requirements: correct count (2 PDFs), correct location (/home/user/Downloads/BlogPosts), and filename matching via multiple strategies.
✅ Postconfig ensures state accessibility: Postconfig installs required dependencies (PyMuPDF, requests) and waits for CDP to be available on port 9222.

✅ Multi-strategy verification: Metric uses multiple matching strategies including filename fuzzy matching, significant word coverage, and PDF content title extraction via PyMuPDF metadata/first page text.

⚠️ Minor: If both CDP and accessibility tree extraction fail, article_titles will be empty and verification returns 0.0. This is semantically correct (cannot verify without knowing actual titles) but could be improved with better error handling or alternative title extraction methods.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding error logging or returning diagnostic information when title extraction fails, to help debug issues in production.
Could add a retry mechanism for CDP connection in case of transient network issues.
Consider validating that extracted PDF titles (from metadata/content) actually match the article titles as an additional verification layer.
